title: The Charge Raised on a Protection Plan for Being Given Up
content:
The charge raised on a Pass and Trip Protection plan for being given up is the plan's cancellation fee, and it
is never below zero.

**The part of the fee the charge stands at.** The part of the fee the charge stands at is the whole of it.

**How much of the term has run.** The part of the term that has run is measured against the days from the day
cover began to the day cover is due to end.

**The least amount kept.** The collective keeps a least amount on a plan given up, which is nothing.

**The greater of the two.** The charge is the greater of the part of the fee the charge stands at and the
least amount the collective keeps, and the greater of the two is taken before anything is allowed against it.

**The allowance.** An allowance is then made against the charge, which is nothing. The allowance is taken off
the greater of the two amounts above and never off the plan's cancellation fee before that comparison, and the
result is rounded to the cent and never falls below zero.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan whose cancellation fee is 45.00 USD. The part of the fee
the charge stands at is the whole of it, 45.00 USD. The least amount the collective keeps is nothing. The
greater of the two is 45.00 USD. The allowance made against it is nothing, so the charge raised is 45.00 USD
once rounded to the cent.

**A second example (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan whose cancellation fee is 15.00 USD. The greater of
the whole fee and the least amount kept is 15.00 USD, and with nothing allowed against it the charge raised is
15.00 USD.
